Poole Harbour

Europes largest natural harbour combines a narrow, fast-running entrance with broad sheltered water, working shipping channels, islands, quiet areas and a dense cluster of marinas.

CRUISING AREA · POOLE HARBOUR

Welcome to Poole Harbour

Poole Harbour changes character the moment a boat clears its narrow entrance. Outside, the approach demands attention to buoyage, commercial traffic, the chain ferry and strong tidal streams; inside, the water opens into a large, sheltered cruising ground shaped by shallow banks, islands, nature reserves, moorings and working channels.

Cobb's Quay Marina

OLD SEA DOGS GUIDES

Cobb's Quay Marina

A large, full-service MDL marina in Holes Bay, reached through Pooles lifting bridges and offering visitor berths, fuel, boatyard support and extensive shore-side services.

MARINA · POOLE HARBOUR

Welcome to Cobb's Quay Marina

Cobbs Quay is the big inner-harbour marina: less about stepping straight into Pooles Old Town and more about having almost every practical boating service close at hand. Reaching it means continuing beyond Poole Quay and transiting the lifting bridges into Holes Bay.

Jump to section
VHF CHANNEL
80
TIDAL INFORMATION
Bridge timing and inner-harbour water levels should be checked before arrival; consult PHC tide and bridge information.
BERTHS
850 marina berths are listed by MDL.
VISITOR BERTHS
Daily visitor and short-stay berthing are offered, subject to availability.
FUEL
Petrol, diesel and gas are listed.
LAUNDRY
Laundry facilities are listed.
WI-FI
MDL WiFi is listed.
REPAIRS
Boat repairs and storage ashore are listed.
CHANDLERY
On-site chandlery is listed.
CRANE / LIFT
MDL lists a 40-ton boat hoist.
RESTAURANTS
Cobbs Bar & Kitchen is listed.
SHOPS
A convenience store and new-boat sales are listed.
Setting & Character

MDL lists 850 marina berths and 280 dry-stack berths, making Cobbs Quay one of Poole Harbours largest marina complexes. It sits in Hamworthy, inside Holes Bay.

Arrival by Sea

MDL directs boats into Poole Harbour by the Swash Channel or, when suitable, the shallower East Looe route, then up-harbour by North Channel or Middle Ship Channel. Pass Poole Quay, transit the lifting bridges and follow the buoyed channel to the marina.

Berthing Experience

Visitor and short-stay berthing are offered. Call Cobbs Quay on VHF Channel 80 or telephone before arrival to confirm availability and instructions.

Facilities

The official visitor guide lists petrol and diesel fuel, gas, 40-ton boat hoist, storage ashore, slipway, repairs, chandlery, convenience store, laundry, restaurant, brokerage, new-boat sales, jet-ski pods, MDL WiFi and 24/7 storage.

Ashore

The marina has its own restaurant and convenience services, while Poole town centre is farther away than from the Town Quay marinas.

Best For

Boats needing a comprehensive marina and boatyard base, dry-stack options or practical servicing during a Poole stay.

Less Suitable For

Crews wanting immediate access to Poole Old Town, or those who do not want to plan around lifting-bridge transits.

Nearby Cruising

The marina opens onto Holes Bay and the wider harbour, with Poole Quay, Brownsea Island and the outer harbour reached back through the marked channels.

OLD SEA DOGS GUIDES

Poole Harbour

Europes largest natural harbour combines a narrow, fast-running entrance with broad sheltered water, working shipping channels, islands, quiet areas and a dense cluster of marinas.

CRUISING AREA · POOLE HARBOUR

Welcome to Poole Harbour

Poole Harbour changes character the moment a boat clears its narrow entrance. Outside, the approach demands attention to buoyage, commercial traffic, the chain ferry and strong tidal streams; inside, the water opens into a large, sheltered cruising ground shaped by shallow banks, islands, nature reserves, moorings and working channels.

Warnings
VHF CHANNEL
14
DEPTHS AND DRAUGHT
PHC's standing East Looe Cut notice gives a conservative passage-planning controlling depth of 0.7m below Chart Datum for the cut; depths elsewhere vary by marked channel and tide.
TIDAL INFORMATION
The harbour entrance has strong tidal streams, particularly at springs. Check current PHC tide data and plan the entrance accordingly.
Setting & Character

Poole Harbour Commissioners describe Poole as Europes largest natural harbour. Its sheltered waters are shared by leisure craft, commercial shipping, ferries, watersports and internationally protected wildlife habitats.

Much of the inner harbour is shallow, while marked channels carry deeper-draught traffic. The result is a cruising area with plenty of room, but one where channel discipline and tide awareness matter.

Arrival by Sea

The Swash Channel is the principal marked approach and the sensible default for unfamiliar crews. Poole VTS uses VHF Channel 14, and PHC advises harbour users to maintain awareness of shipping movements before getting underway or entering the approaches.

The East Looe Cut is a secondary shortcut from the east. PHCs standing notice says it should be used only with caution, with under-keel clearance calculated carefully; for passage planning PHC gives a controlling depth of 0.7 metres below Chart Datum and warns that the sands move and buoy positions can lag sudden changes.

At the harbour entrance, give way to the chain ferry. PHC and BCP guidance both stress the narrow entrance, strong tidal streams and the need to pass well clear astern of the ferry.

Inside the Harbour

Once inside, the main channels lead toward Poole Quay, the Port of Poole, Hamworthy, Holes Bay and the Wareham Channel. Small craft must stay alert around the harbour entrance precautionary area, blind bends and large commercial vessel movements.

Speed limits and quiet areas vary around the harbour. The general harbour limit is 10 knots, with 6-knot limits in Little Channel and Holes Bay and additional quiet-area restrictions.

Where to Berth

Visitor options range from Poole Quay Boat Haven on the town waterfront to larger and more sheltered facilities farther inside. This collection covers Poole Quay Boat Haven, Port of Poole Marina, Cobbs Quay Marina, Salterns Marina, Parkstone Bay Marina and Lake Yard Marina.

The marinas differ markedly in access, depth, visitor availability and shore-side atmosphere, so berth choice should be made against the vessels draught, bridge requirements and intended time ashore.

Sandbanks & Brownsea Island

Sandbanks forms the eastern side of the harbour entrance and is an unmistakable landfall. Brownsea Island dominates the inner harbour; private craft may land only on the South Shore under National Trust rules, with no landing on the North Shore, sea wall or National Trust pier.

Best For

Crews looking for sheltered cruising, a choice of marinas, short hops between anchorages and easy access to Poole, Brownsea Island, Studland and the Dorset coast.

Less Suitable For

Skippers who are unwilling to plan around commercial traffic, strong tidal streams, shallow inner-harbour water or changing local navigation notices.

Nearby Cruising

Studland Bay and Old Harry Rocks lie immediately outside the entrance, with Swanage and the Jurassic Coast farther west. Eastbound, Poole provides a natural stepping stone back toward Christchurch Bay and the Solent.

Skipper's Notes

Listen to Poole VTS on Channel 14, check current shipping movements and Local Notices to Mariners, keep clear of large commercial vessels and give way to the chain ferry.

Do not rely on an old East Looe depth figure: PHC specifically warns that the sands shift and publishes a conservative planning depth for the cut.

Information checked against official sources

Navigation and harbour-safety information in this Draft has been checked against Poole Harbour Commissioners 2026 Harbour Guide, current VTS and shipping information, stand

Poole Quay Boat Haven

Pooles town-quay visitor marina puts boats directly beside the Old Town, restaurants and harbour life, with VHF 80 berthing and strong demand in summer.

MARINA · POOLE HARBOUR

Welcome to Poole Quay Boat Haven

Poole Quay Boat Haven is the most immediate visitor berth for crews who want to step off the pontoon and straight onto Poole Quay. The location is lively rather than secluded, but it gives visiting boats a practical base close to the Old Town and within the wider shelter of Poole Harbour.

VHF CHANNEL

TIDAL INFORMATION
The marina is inside Poole Harbour; passage to it depends on safe transit of the harbour entrance and current harbour conditions.
VISITOR BERTHS
Visitor berths and short-stay berths are available; advance booking is recommended during the summer season.
WATER
Drinking water is provided on all pontoons.
ELECTRICITY
16A shore power is available on all pontoons, with higher-amperage supplies on a limited number of berths.
SHOWERS
Showers are available to berth holders and visitors.
TOILETS
Toilets are available to berth holders and visitors, including accessible provision.
LAUNDRY
Laundry facilities are available; tokens are purchased from reception.
RESTAURANTS
Poole Quay restaurants and cafés are immediately outside the marina.
BARS
Poole Quay bars and pubs are immediately accessible ashore.
Setting & Character

The Boat Haven sits directly on Poole Quay, opposite the harbour and within walking distance of the Old Town, cafs, bars and restaurants. It is a visitor-focused marina with a busy summer season.

Arrival by Sea

Enter Poole Harbour using current PHC directions, maintain awareness of VHF Channel 14 shipping broadcasts, then proceed to Poole Quay. Call Poole Quay Boat Haven on VHF Channel 80 when nearing the marina; staff allocate the berth on the day of arrival.

Berthing Experience

Visitor berths are heavily used in summer and the operator recommends advance booking. Short stays of up to four hours are offered at Poole Quay Boat Haven, subject to space and allocation on arrival.

Facilities

The operator lists drinking water on all pontoons, shore power, showers, toilets and laundry. Pump-out is available near the Haven entrance but may be obstructed by working-berth activity, so advance contact is recommended.

Ashore

The marinas great advantage is the quay itself: shops, pubs, cafs, restaurants, harbour cruises and Pooles historic centre are immediately accessible on foot.

Best For

Crews prioritising a central Poole berth, easy access ashore and a lively waterfront stop.

Less Suitable For

Those seeking a quiet marina setting, or crews arriving in peak summer without a reservation.

Nearby Cruising

Brownsea Island, Sandbanks, Studland Bay and the wider inner harbour are all close enough for short local passages.

Skipper's Notes

Book ahead in summer, call VHF 80 on approach, and continue to monitor PHC navigation information for the harbour entrance and commercial traffic.

Information checked against official sources

Berthing, VHF, facilities and contact details were checked against Poole Quay Boat Havens current official information and PHC harbour-safety sources.

Enter Poole Harbour in accordance with current PHC Harbour Guide and Local Notices to Mariners.

Proceed toward Poole Quay while remaining alert to commercial traffic.

Call 'Poole Quay Boat Haven' on VHF Channel 80 when nearing the marina for berth allocation.

Tidal information

The marina is inside Poole Harbour; passage to it depends on safe transit of the harbour entrance and current harbour conditions.

Hazards and cautions

Commercial traffic in the harbour approaches and channels.

Busy visitor traffic around Poole Quay.

Practical notes

Advance booking is recommended in summer. Berths are allocated on the day of arrival; contact the marina as you near Poole Quay.

Old Sea Dogs View

For a first night in Poole, the Boat Haven is hard to beat for convenience. The trade-off is obvious: this is the harbours front row, not its quiet corner. Arrive with the berth organised and the evening ashore takes care of itself.

OLD SEA DOGS GUIDES

Sandbanks

The sandy peninsula at Poole Harbours entrance is both a major local landmark and one of Dorsets best-known beaches, with the chain ferry and fast harbour stream immediately alongside.

DESTINATION · POOLE HARBOUR

Welcome to Sandbanks

Sandbanks is the landform every Poole arrival notices. The peninsula forms the eastern side of the narrow harbour entrance, placing beach life, waterfront property and one of the harbours busiest navigation pinch-points within a few hundred metres of each other.

In this Guide
Setting & Character
Arrival by Sea
Berthing Experience
Facilities
Ashore
Best For
Less Suitable For
Nearby Cruising
Skipper's Notes
Information checked against official sources
Approach and arrival
Tidal information
Hazards and cautions
Practical notes
Old Sea Dogs View
Warnings
TIDAL INFORMATION
Strong tidal streams occur at the narrow harbour entrance, especially at springs.
Setting & Character

BCP Council describes Sandbanks as an award-winning beach with golden sand, cafs, toilets, showers and seasonal lifeguards. For boaters, its importance is just as much geographical: it marks one side of Poole Harbours narrow entrance.

Arrival by Sea

Treat Sandbanks primarily as an entrance landmark, not as an invitation to improvise a landing. PHC and BCP guidance describe the harbour entrance as potentially hazardous because of strong tidal streams, commercial traffic and the chain ferry.

Berthing Experience

This Guide does not claim a public visitor berth or landing at Sandbanks. Use a recognised marina, mooring or authorised landing arrangement and confirm local access before going ashore by boat.

Facilities

The public beach has toilets, accessible facilities, drinking water, showers, caf/kiosk services and seasonal lifeguards.

Ashore

Sandbanks is a beach destination first: a long sandy frontage, watersports, cafs and views toward Studland and the Purbeck coast.

Best For

Crews using Sandbanks as a harbour landmark or visiting the peninsula ashore from a confirmed berth or authorised landing arrangement.

Less Suitable For

Anyone treating the busy harbour entrance or ferry approaches as casual anchoring or landing water.

Nearby Cruising

Brownsea Island is immediately inside the harbour, with Studland Bay and Old Harry Rocks outside to the south-west.

Skipper's Notes

Give way to the chain ferry, expect strong stream at the entrance and follow current PHC navigation directions.

Information checked against official sources

Shore-side information was checked against BCP Council and Poole Tourism; harbour-entry safety comes from current PHC/BCP guidance.

Approach and arrival

Use Sandbanks as a visual landmark while following the charted Poole Harbour approach and current PHC directions.

At the harbour entrance, give way to the chain ferry and pass well clear astern.

Tidal information

Strong tidal streams occur at the narrow harbour entrance, especially at springs.

Hazards and cautions

Chain ferry at the harbour entrance.

Strong tidal stream in the narrow entrance.

Commercial and leisure traffic concentration.

Practical notes

No public visitor berth or general private-boat landing arrangement was established in the checked official sources.

Old Sea Dogs View

Sandbanks is useful to a skipper because it is impossible to miss. It is also a reminder that Pooles most glamorous shoreline sits beside its most concentrated piece of navigation. Enjoy the landmark, but keep the seamanship switched on until the ferry and entrance are astern.

Warnings

Use the latest Poole Harbour Commissioners Harbour Guide, Local Notices to Mariners, shipping movements, tide information and marina instructions before arrival.

OLD SEA DOGS GUIDES

Brownsea Island

Poole Harbours wooded island is a natural cruising landmark and a destination in its own right, with private-craft landing permitted only on the South Shore under National Trust rules.

DESTINATION · POOLE HARBOUR

Welcome to Brownsea Island

Brownsea Island sits at the heart of Poole Harbour, dividing channels and views while giving visiting crews a rare chance to turn a harbour passage into a walk through woodland, heath and shoreline nature reserve.

Setting & Character

The National Trust manages Brownsea as a protected island nature reserve known for red squirrels, woodland, heath and harbour views.

Arrival by Sea

Private boats, kayaks and paddleboards are welcome to land only along the South Shore. The National Trust states that there is no landing along the North Shore or sea wall because of nesting birds, and no private landing at the National Trust pier for safety.

Berthing Experience

Brownsea is a landing destination rather than a marina. Skippers must make their own safe anchoring/mooring arrangements in accordance with current harbour rules and then use only permitted landing areas.

Facilities

The island has visitor reception, caf facilities, toilets and visitor services during opening periods. Passenger ferries also operate from Poole Quay.

Ashore

Brownsea offers walking, wildlife watching and harbour views. The National Trusts current visitor information should be checked for opening times, admission and seasonal arrangements before landing.

Best For

Crews wanting to add a genuine shore excursion and nature stop to a Poole Harbour day.

Less Suitable For

Anyone expecting marina facilities, unrestricted landing around the island or access outside current National Trust opening arrangements.

Nearby Cruising

Sandbanks lies east at the harbour entrance, Poole Quay to the north-east and the quieter western harbour toward Arne and the Wareham Channel.

Skipper's Notes

Land on the South Shore only. Do not use the National Trust pier for private landing, and respect the no-landing North Shore and sea-wall restrictions.

Information checked against official sources

Landing rules and visitor information were checked against the National Trusts current Brownsea Island guidance, with wider navigation context from PHC.

Approach and arrival

Navigate within Poole Harbour under current PHC guidance and select a safe anchoring/mooring arrangement outside navigational channels.

For private craft, land on Brownsea Island's South Shore only.

Do not land on the North Shore, sea wall or at the National Trust pier.

Hazards and cautions

Protected no-landing areas on the North Shore and sea wall.

Passenger ferry operations at the National Trust pier.

Shallow water and channels around the island require current charted navigation.

Practical notes

Check National Trust opening information and current PHC harbour guidance before planning a private-boat landing.

Old Sea Dogs View

Brownsea is the rare harbour landmark that deserves to become the destination. The attraction for a cruising crew is not complicated: secure the boat properly, respect the landing rules and go ashore for a few hours. It changes the character of a Poole stop completely.

Warnings

Use the latest Poole Harbour Commissioners Harbour Guide, Local Notices to Mariners, shipping movements, tide information and marina instructions before arrival.

Private craft may land on Brownsea Islands South Shore only; the North Shore, sea wall and National Trust pier are not private-craft landing points.
